mechanics.fact: Both decks need at least one player rider; while both have riders the direction is determined by difference in total load, with each player and Gem contributing weight 1. Thus Pac can place Gem on A and ride too to make A heavier and raise B.

evidence.claim: Each player contributes weight 1; the paired lifts move only with a rider on both decks, in the direction determined by their load difference.

mechanics.fact: Gem emits periodic bubbles toward the fixed target; Isp receives FLOAT and Pac receives STICKY, while Pac can also bounce off a bubble from above. FLOAT temporarily prevents jump input and STICKY blocks Pac movement.

evidence.claim: Gem fires a bubble at a fixed target with a 0.9 second windup and 1 second cooldown.
A bubble hit gives Isp FLOAT and Pac STICKY; these are temporary status effects.
FLOAT blocks jumping and STICKY blocks horizontal motion while active.

mechanics.fact: The upper route is a continuous fold over a shaft wall; the ground-level floor runs across the room, so a missed upper transfer is not automatically a lethal fall.

evidence.claim: The room defines a continuous safe floor, counterweight decks, continuous shaft walls, upper fold, two exits, no authored hazards, and no collectibles.

confidence_reason: Current authored mechanics and ordinary-input success/recovery traces establish a feasible mandatory both-exit route and bounded recoveries. They do not measure first-time human discovery, shared-keyboard reliability, enjoyment, or general floor-fall recovery.

confirmed: The subtitle and visible load panel point toward Gem weight, both decks, and a bubble; the full route indeed uses all three.
Both heroes must contribute distinct roles, as first-pass cooperation estimated.
There is no narrow one-shot window; a missed bubble can be retried.
missed_mechanics: Gem is an active weight-1 villain body; Pac pushes him onto deck A, making A load 2 while Isp rides B at load 1.
The bubble gives Isp FLOAT and Pac STICKY; the Isp effect is the upper lift, while Pac takes the low passage.
A continuous floor and static containment make the tested missed transfer and over-push recoverable without death.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass described the B indicator changing without keys as uncertain animation/state; current replay shows that the idle capture was coincident with Gem attacking and the deck indicator responding to dynamic room simulation, not player input. The first-pass uncertainty was appropriate, not a false control claim.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 2 to 3 because a three-part causal route is required: paired rider condition, load asymmetry from Gem, and timed FLOAT catch followed by split paths.
Timing rises from 0 to 2 because bubble firing creates a repeatable intercept window and missed catches can be retried.
Hazards resolves from null to 0 because the mandatory fall/expiry evidence shows safe continuous floor and no authored damaging hazards; the missed upper transfer is recoverable.
Recovery cost resolves from null to 1 because two distinct scripted mistakes recover, though one adds substantial regroup time.
Solution clarity remains 2: source reveals a full hint, but the unassisted subtitle and board still omit key causal links.
unresolved: No human first encounter establishes whether players infer the Gem-weight interaction or intercept the bubble.
General floor-fall recovery and actual two-human control friction are untested.

single_operator_note: One operator would need to coordinate two different movement key groups while also watching a periodic bubble; this additional interference is not included in the two-human baseline.
